data.headline: Arabica falls to 266.45 cents/lb as currency depreciation and expanding Brazilian exports weigh heavily on global prices.
data.price_action: Coffee closed at 266.45 cents/lb as of November 10, 2026, down 6.2% over the past week and 9.0% over the past month. Prices are currently depressed at the 4.8th percentile of their 52-week range. Recent annualized volatility stands at 31.8%, below the historical average of 40.7%.
key_developments: Expanding and soaring Brazilian coffee export shipments continue to undercut Arabica prices as export supplies build (source: 441175f168c85349, f9bfa07ffbc3c4d4).

Extreme Brazilian real weakness (BRL/USD at 5.7815, up 13.4% over the month and at its 100.0th 1-year percentile) is heavily incentivizing producer sales and export pace, putting consistent downward pressure on prices (source: 4903c96cce17a056, f63f64eb858b3f79).
Trader expectations of larger, expanding Brazilian coffee exports are continuing to drag futures lower (source: 6278b6d807d4564d, 6d5d7db029d703d4).
data.weather_crop: Brazil is in its critical flowering stage where seasonal frost risk carries high impact, though 0 frost days were recorded in the past week. Conditions are drier than normal with a dryness z-score of +0.76 and 30-day rainfall at 149.6 mm. Concurrently, Vietnam has entered its harvest phase.
